shadows.name: part-on-board

shadows.name: part-lifted

shadows.name: board-on-desk
shadows.purpose: The board, search palette, overlays, lone panels (--sh-3).

shadows.name: signal-halo
shadows.purpose: Live LED (2px), probe tip (3px), current slide via (4px), live net pad (5px).

shadows.name: signal-trace-glow

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Reference easing; hovers, lifts, bar hide, chevrons.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrances: digit roll, slide, palette, overlay.

motion.name: signal-pulse
motion.value: 46px white dash along the live trace; duration max(1800ms, 2.2ms per px); linear; infinite; travels 0–78% then rests
motion.purpose: The one authored ambient motion. Not started when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches.

motion.name: digit-roll
motion.value: 0.42s ease-out, translateY(-55%) and opacity 0 to rest
motion.purpose: An instrument digit that changed value rolls in once.

motion.name: slide-in
motion.value: 0.35s ease-out, translateY(8px) and opacity 0 to rest

motion.name: panel-in
motion.value: 0.16s–0.18s ease-out, translateY(-6px) and opacity 0 to rest

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition durations 0.001ms, one iteration

narrative.overview:
The course is one circuit board, and a penetration test is a signal routed through it. Every session is a component soldered onto a single bus; pivoting is a via down to an inner layer; validating a claim is probing a test point; a path that has not been proven yet is a thin ratsnest line until it becomes routed copper. The student reads their own progress as how far the signal has travelled. This world replaces the retired Blueprint Console in full: there is no ruled grid background, no corner ticks, no gradient text and no mono eyebrow above headings.

Three inks own the page, all taken from the CODED reference (https://coded-reels-playbook.vercel.app/): navy solder mask, gold copper and white silkscreen. Cyan is the fourth ink and the rarest. On the board, the diagrams and the chrome it means only "live signal": the powered trace, the travelling pulse, the active probe, the focus ring. The board sits on a darker desk (#00081c), so the solder mask reads as a physical object with mounting holes, edge connectors and a silkscreened part number. The world stays recognisable with all content removed: orthogonal traces with 45-degree chamfers, gold pad rows on chip bodies, round vias with a dark drill hole, mounting holes and silkscreen outlines.

Density is a working instrument, not a poster. A compact headline band (one claim, two actions, one probe readout) sits above a board that fills the rest of the first viewport. Study mode reads as a component datasheet. Presenter mode gives the slide the whole screen and shows progress as a trace with one via per slide. The print path swaps to white stock with navy ink. The world refuses the hacker-terminal costume (phosphor green, Matrix rain, fake CLI chrome) and the generic dark dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Three inks (navy mask, gold copper, white silkscreen); cyan is reserved for the live signal on the board and in the chrome.
Every connection is drawn in one of three states: proven (solid cyan), probing (dotted cyan) or ratsnest (thin dashed copper, or dashed blue on the inner layer).
Theory sessions are IC chips with designator `U#`; labs are test headers with designator `J#`.
Silkscreen type (IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, tracked) carries functional data only and always sits on the same row as what it labels.
Semantic colour lives inside the teaching content and is always paired with an icon and a word.
One ambient motion, the signal pulse, turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Navy solder mask, gold copper and white silkscreen own every surface. Any other colour on screen is either the live signal or a labelled semantic channel inside teaching content.

rules.name: The Live Signal Rule
rules.body: On the board, the diagrams' state and the chrome, cyan means only "the signal has reached here" or "you are here": proven trace, probing segment, pulse, active probe, focus, current slide. Never use it as decoration, as a heading colour or as a background fill.

rules.name: The Icon-and-Word Rule
rules.body: A semantic channel is never carried by colour alone. Callouts pair the channel's icon with its word (Evidence, Attacker, Validated, Caution, Network, Identity); list items, steps and pinout rows pair a coloured pad or ring with text; LEDs always sit next to a state word.

rules.name: The Reference-Only Rule
rules.body: Every colour comes from the CODED reference palette. Do not invent navies, panel tints or in-between values; if a surface needs a navy, it is one of the reference navies.

rules.name: The Silkscreen Rule
rules.body: Mono uppercase text is functional data printed on the part, never a kicker. Designators and tags sit on the heading row (probe title row, datasheet section row, reference stage heading) or in a slide's silkscreen footer. Never stack a label above a heading.

rules.name: The Legibility Floor Rule
rules.body: No HTML text below 0.75rem and no SVG text below 12px. Silkscreen gets small by being 0.75rem and tracked, never by going smaller.

rules.name: The Plain Claim Rule
rules.body: Headlines are plain, bold, tightly tracked sans: no gradient fill, no outline type, no glow, no mono display.

rules.name: The Parts Sit On The Board Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this component is soldered on top". Chips get it; test headers, panels and tables do not. Shadows always fall downward and are tinted navy-black, never grey and never zero-offset.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Only the signal glows. Apart from the gold pad under the primary button, no element gets a coloured halo.

rules.name: The Chamfer Rule
rules.body: Every routed line is orthogonal with 45-degree corner cuts. No bezier curves and no free diagonals.

rules.name: The Through-Hole Rule
rules.body: A circle on this board is a hole or a pad: it has a copper ring and a dark centre, or it is a solid copper or signal dot. Never use a circle as a generic avatar or decoration.

rules.name: The One Pulse Rule
rules.body: The only authored ambient motion is the signal pulse: a 46px white dash that travels the live trace once every max(1.8s, 2.2ms per px) on a linear loop with a pause at the end. It is checked against `prefers-reduced-motion` before it starts and never runs when the user reduces motion. Everything else is a response to a state change: digit roll (0.42s), slide entrance (0.35s, 8px rise), palette and overlay entrance (0.16 to 0.18s), hover lifts and colour transitions (0.15 to 0.2s) on `cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1)`. A global reduced-motion rule cuts all of these to near zero.

dos: Do build every surface from the three inks: solder mask #00112f on desk #00081c, gold copper #e0b45c / #c89a45, silkscreen #ffffff.
Do spend cyan #79e2ec only where the signal is live or where the user is now (on the board, diagrams and chrome); inside teaching content it is the Network channel, with icon and word.
Do draw every connection in one of the three states (proven solid cyan, probing dotted cyan, ratsnest dashed copper or inner-layer blue) and drop a via at each layer or week crossing.
Do designate theory as `U#` chips and labs as `J#` headers wherever a session is named (board, probe, datasheet, presenter, pager).
Do put silkscreen designators and tags on the heading row or in the slide's silkscreen footer.
Do pair every semantic colour with its icon and its word (Evidence, Attacker, Validated, Caution, Network, Identity).
Do keep HTML text at 0.75rem or larger and SVG text at 12px or larger.
Do keep muted-2 #6f83a8 text on the solder mask or the desk; on raised component bodies use muted #9fb2d4.
Do show counts as zero-padded copper instrument digits that roll only when the value changes.
Do keep the print path as white stock and navy ink, with the print-safe reference values for each channel.
donts: Don't bring back the Blueprint Console: no ruled grid or graticule background, no corner tick marks, no mono eyebrow stacked above a heading.
Don't set any text in a gradient, including a single hero word.
Don't dress the page in the hacker-terminal costume: phosphor green, Matrix rain, scanlines, blinking cursors. Console wells are teaching content showing real commands, not a page style.
Don't introduce colours outside the CODED reference palette; no invented in-between navies.
Don't use cyan as decoration, for headings or as a large fill; don't let red become the dominant colour or carry meaning alone.
Don't route lines with curves or free diagonals; corners are 45-degree chamfers.
Don't add looping or ambient motion beyond the signal pulse, and never run the pulse under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Don't give flat panels, tables or test headers a drop shadow; only raised parts cast one.
